ambiguities_or_notes: Every source block (29) has a matching target block, with page markers, numbering, quotation structure, and italics preserved.

Website Circle of Reading paragraphs served as the first draft; each was re-read against the Russian and revised where it drifted (omissions, additions, generic he/his, terminology, attribution form).

Attributions follow the print: «Мади» (Madi) is kept as printed though the Kufa story is Saadi's (Gulistan); «Карлейль» is Carlyle (surname only); the English title of the proverb collection is kept as Tolstoy printed it. «Роптать» (roptat', 'murmur') and «положение» (polozhenie, 'situation') are kept in their repetitions.

Source observation: [8] attribution printed «Мади» (Madi); the story of the man without legs in the mosque of Kufa is from Saadi's Gulistan, so «Мади» is probably a misprint for «Саади»; kept as printed
Source observation: [12] attribution «Лao-Tce» is typed with Latin a, o, T, c, e mixed into the Cyrillic (transcription slip); rendered Laozi
